page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and Intel Xeon 8369B processors clocked at 2.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Cache hierarchy includes 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Hardware resource allocations do not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring persistent data to be attached via network block storage. Networking capability features a baseline throughput of 10 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Synthetic benchmarks position the instance within the middle 50 percent across standard metrics, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 9,153, a multi-core stress-ng score of 15,477.28, and a PassMark CPU rating of 20,865.11.

Memory throughput registers at 93.71 GB/s for large-block uncached reads and 53.88 GB/s for large-block writes. Application workloads show balanced mid-tier throughput, such as 15.34 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 18.93 GB/s in static web serving. For lightweight machine learning inference, prompt processing reaches 1,281.68 tokens per second on small 135M models, but drops to a weaker tier of 31.09 tokens per second on medium 7B models.

By delivering dedicated compute cores paired with a compact memory footprint and baseline 10 Gbps networking, the instance offers cost-efficient compute density without the overhead of surplus RAM or unneeded local disks. The profile fits CPU-bound workloads such as web application hosting, build systems, Clang software compilation, Redis caching tiers, and medium-scale data processing pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz across 8 physical cores. Configured with 32.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio suitable for processing-heavy workloads. The platform includes AVX-512 with VNNI and hardware cryptographic acceleration, alongside a 10 Gbps baseline network interface. It includes no bundled local storage or discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks position the instance in the middle 50 percent for general compute and memory bandwidth, scoring 20,865.11 in PassMark CPU and 9,153 in multi-core Geekbench. In-memory operations reach 15.34 million Redis SET operations per second, with web serving reaching 18.93 GB/s. Due to its lean memory profile and absence of local disks, it is well suited for stateless web clusters, code compilation, continuous integration pipelines, and front-end network services.
